promptState.text: A cute cartoon 3D render of a fluffy white bunny in a Pixar-like style, a close-up portrait from the chest up. It has big shiny dark eyes, rosy cheeks and a small happy smile, and wears an orange hoodie with the word "PIXA" printed in white on the chest. Warm window light from the left, a cozy room softly blurred behind, shallow depth of field.

widgets_values:
{"version": 1, "content": "

WHAT EACH NODE DOES

The colour of a node tells you what kind of node it is. Nothing here needs changing except the blue ones.

 Models to download

Orange. Each one needs a file from the list in the note above.

  • Load Diffusion Model (Qwen Image 2.1) - The image model itself, 7B, from Alibaba's Qwen team.
  • Load CLIP (Qwen3-VL 8B) - Reads your prompt.
  • Load VAE - Turns the finished render into a picture. It works with four channels, red, green, blue and transparency, which is how this model can make transparent pictures.
  • LoRA Loader Pixaroma - Adds Viggle's turbo LoRA, which lets the model finish a picture in 6 steps instead of 25. It has no trigger word. Keep it at strength 1.

 The speed node

Teal, above the graph.

  • Model Attention Backend - Set to comfy kitchen attention, a faster way to do the model's attention maths. It changes the speed, not the picture. The note on the right has the numbers. On a graphics card that cannot use it, ComfyUI falls back to normal attention by itself.

 The numbers you set

Blue, and numbered. These are the only nodes you have to touch.

  • 1. Pick Orientation and Size - The size of the picture. The starred sizes are the native 2K sizes Qwen lists for this model; the others are smaller and much faster. For video, 1920 x 1088 is Full HD (the model works in steps of 16 pixels, so 1080 becomes 1088) and 2560 x 1440 is 1440p. The orientation switch flips a size between portrait and landscape.
  • 2. Add a prompt - What you want to see. Put any words you want written in the picture in quotes, like the word on the hoodie in the demo prompt.
  • 3. Seed Random/Fixed? - Fixed repeats the same picture, Random rolls a new one each Run.

 The helper

Purple, under the size node.

  • ModelSamplingFlux - Spaces the 6 steps for the picture's size, the way the turbo LoRA was trained, so it reads the width and height from step 1. The name says Flux because the maths is the same. Its two numbers are set for this LoRA (max shift 0.69, base shift 0.5): leave them.

 The render

Green. These run by themselves.

  • Text Encode Qwen Image 2.1 - Reads your prompt through the text encoder. It has a negative prompt box, but that does nothing at CFG 1, the setting this model is made for, so leave it empty.
  • Empty Latent Image - The blank canvas, at the size from step 1.
  • RandomNoise, KSamplerSelect, BasicScheduler, ExtendIntermediateSigmas, Basic Guider, SamplerCustomAdvanced - Together they do the job of a KSampler, with the 6 steps the turbo LoRA wants. BasicScheduler makes the 4 steps the LoRA was trained on, and ExtendIntermediateSigmas cuts the first, biggest one into three. Basic Guider means CFG 1, the setting this model is made for, so there is no negative prompt. Leave their numbers as they are.
  • VAE Decode - Turns the finished render into a picture.

 The result

Dark red, at the end.

  • Preview Image Pixaroma - Shows the picture and saves it to your output folder as a PNG. PNG keeps transparency, so a transparent picture stays transparent.

The dark Run Timer above it shows how long the last Run took. Handy when you are trying sizes against the table in the other note.

widgets_values:
{"version": 1, "content": "

SETTINGS AND RUN TIME

 What this workflow makes

The Text to Image workflow in 6 steps instead of 25, with Viggle's turbo LoRA: about three times as fast at 2K, with pictures that look almost the same.

Tested on 8 seeds with the demo prompt, each against the normal 25-step workflow on the same seed: the turbo drew the same bunny in the same room every time, just as sharp, and in the same pose on 7 of the 8. The word on the hoodie came out right on 7 of the 8 seeds, against all 8 at 25 steps.

Every number below was measured on a 24 GB RTX 4090 with this workflow and its own settings, each run on a fresh seed with the models already loaded. A different card gives different numbers, but the shape holds: the cost goes up with the pixels.

 How long a Run takes

SizePixelsTurbo, 6 stepsNormal, 25 steps
832 x 1248about 1 MP, the default2 s5 s
1024 x 1024about 1 MP2 s5 s
1088 x 1920Full HD, about 2.1 MP3 s10 s
1536 x 1536about 2.4 MP4 s12 s
1440 x 25601440p, about 3.7 MP6 s21 s
1696 x 2528native 2K, 4.3 MP8 s26 s

The normal column is the Text to Image workflow in this folder, measured in the same session. The first Run with the turbo LoRA also has to load it; the table is the Runs after that.

 Video sizes: Full HD and 1440p

Full HD is 1088 x 1920 in portrait and 1920 x 1088 in landscape. The model works in steps of 16 pixels, so 1080 is not possible: asking for 1080 gives exactly the same 1088 picture. For an exact 1080, trim 8 pixels. 1440p, 1440 x 2560 or 2560 x 1440, divides evenly and comes out exact.

 When to use the normal workflow

Text is the turbo's weak spot: Viggle's model card says small or long text comes out garbled more often than at 25 steps, and the one miss above was the word on the hoodie. For a picture that has to carry a lot of text, use the normal Text to Image workflow. For everything else, the turbo is the quick way to try prompts and seeds.

 Why the six green sampler nodes

The turbo LoRA was trained on 4 steps, and Viggle recommends cutting the first, biggest step into three: 6 steps. A plain KSampler cannot space steps like that. Tested on the same 8 seeds: a KSampler at 4 steps gave softer, hazier pictures, and at 8 steps the fur came out grainy. The six nodes here gave the pictures closest to Viggle's own 6 steps.

ModelSamplingFlux matters at the big sizes: without it the 2K pictures came out with grainy fur.

 Kitchen attention

The teal Model Attention Backend node is set to comfy kitchen attention, a faster way to do the attention maths. On the same seed at 1696 x 2528, it took 8 s, against 11 s with the normal pytorch attention, and the two pictures came out the same, with small differences in the fine details. To compare it yourself, switch the node to pytorch attention.

It needs an Nvidia or AMD graphics card. On anything else ComfyUI falls back to normal attention by itself, so the workflow still runs.

 The first Run of the session

The first Run after starting ComfyUI has to load 6.8 GB of image model and 8.7 GB of text encoder, plus the turbo LoRA. Measured on an 832 x 1248 picture: 7 s with the models unloaded first, 2 s once they were loaded.

That was with the model files still in this machine's file cache. The very first load after switching the computer on reads them off the disk for real and will be slower; that case was not measured, so no number is given for it.

 What it takes off the card

The graphics card peaked at about 20 GB during these runs, at 1696 x 2528. ComfyUI keeps the models loaded while it has room, so that number says a 24 GB card copes, not how little the model can get by with.

 More

  • The same LoRA also works for image editing, with one to three pictures; that is not in this workflow yet.
  • Viggle's larger rank 256 file works the same way. On the demo prompt it gave practically the same pictures as this rank 128 one, at twice the download.
  • Turbo LoRA model card 
", "buttonColor": "#f66744", "lineColor": "#f66744", "width": 810, "height": 1494, "backgroundColor": "#2a2a2a"}
